questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.**

David said, “Can someone please explain what is going on?”

options.text: David asked that if someone could explain what is going on.
David said can someone please explain what is going on.
David asked whether someone could explain what was going on.
David asked if someone can please explain what was going on.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **David asked whether someone could explain what was going on. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is a direct speech and we need to convert it into an indirect speech.
 
• The given sentence is also an interrogative sentence.
 
• We follow these rules in Direct-Indirect speech for an interrogative sentence:
 
 
• A question mark should always be used at the end of an interrogative sentence in direct speech.
 
• To convert direct speech to indirect speech quotation marks should be replaced by a full stop.
 
• The reporting verb '**said**' changes to '**asked**' in indirect speech.
 
• Interrogative sentence changes to assertive form [direct to indirect speech]
 
• The conjunction ‘that’ is not used to connect the clauses instead of, ‘whether’ is used for the conversion to join the clauses.
 
• The helping verb 'is' changed to 'was' in the indirect part.
 
• The modal '**can**' changes to '**could**' in the indirect speech.
 
• **Inverted commas("...")** are omitted to show the indirect speech part.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct indirect speech: *David asked whether someone could explain what was going on. *

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

I said to the office boy, “Take these papers to the manager immediately.”

options.text: I ordered the office boy to take those papers to the manager immediately.
I said to the office boy to take these papers to the manager immediately.
I requested the office boy to take these papers to the manager immediately.
I told the office boy take those papers to the manager immediately.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **I ordered the office boy to take those papers to the manager immediately**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a direct speech.
 
• The basic rules for changing or ____converting direct speech into indirect speech__:​
 __
 
• The commas and inverted commas are removed and 'to' is added.
 
• The pronoun 'these' becomes 'those'.
 
• The reporting verb '**said**' becomes '**ordered**'.
 
 

Correct sentence:__ ***'I ordered the office boy to take those papers to the manager immediately.'***

questions.question:
Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

She said to her brother, “Who do you think will win the best all-rounder award this year ?”

options.text: She asked to her brother who he thought will win the best all-rounder award that year.
She asked her brother who did he thought would win the best all-rounder award that year.
She asked her brother who he thought would win the best all-rounder award that year.
She asked her brother who did he think will win the best all-rounder award this year.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **She asked her brother who he thought would win the best all-rounder award that year.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a direct speech.
 
• The basic rules for changing or converting direct speech into indirect speech:​
 
 
• The commas, inverted commas and question mark (?) are removed.
 
• The second person pronoun 'you' becomes the third person pronoun 'he'. "This year" becomes "That year".
 
• The present simple tense format 'Subject + V1 (do, think) + Object' will be changed into the past simple tense format 'Subject + (V2​) + Object'.
 
• The future simple tense format 'Subject + will + V1 (win) + Object' will be changed into the present conditional tense format 'Subject + would + V1 (win) + Object'.
 
 

Thus the correct option is Option 3).

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect narration of the given sentence.**

Priya told her mother, “I couldn’t get all the items you wanted today from the shop.”

options.text: Priya told to her mother that I couldn’t get all the items you wanted today from the shop.
Priya told her mother that she couldn’t get all the items I wanted that day from the shop.
Priya told her mother I couldn’t get all the items she wanted today from the shop.
Priya told her mother that she couldn’t get all the items she wanted that day from the shop.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Priya told her mother that she couldn’t get all the items she wanted that day from the shop.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from direct to indirect speech:
 
• When the direct speech is in an assertive form, we follow the steps given below:
 
 
• Convert the sentence in the direct speech into assertive.
 
• The tense of reported speech is changed only when the reporting verb is in the past tense. 
 
• The reporting verb 'told' will remain the same.
 
• The connector 'that' will follow the removal of comma and inverted commas.​
 
• The personal pronouns will be changed according to the subject and object of the reporting verb.
 
• ​Here the 1st person 'I' will change into the 3rd person 'she' as per the object.
 
• The modal verb 'could not' will remain the same.
 
• Words showing time and place are changed accordingly. (today- that day)
 
 
 
• ​​At last line up the remaining part.

 

Following these steps, we get-* Priya told her mother that she couldn’t get all the items she wanted that day from the shop.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Mother said to Kavya, "Switch off the light before you go to sleep."

options.text: Mother told Kavya to switch off the light before she goes to sleep.
Mother told Kavya to switch off the light before she went to sleep.
Mother told Kavya to switch off the light before you go to sleep.
Mother told Kavya to switch off the light before she is going to sleep.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Mother told Kavya to switch off the light before she went to sleep'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **Direct Speech.** As per the given question we have to change it into **Indirect Speech. **
 
• The process of transformation as follows: ​
 
 
• The given sentence is an example of an Imperative Sentence. 
 
• Transformation of Imperative Sentence. 
 
• 'Orders', 'Command', 'Request', 'Advice' are given in these kinds of sentences. 
 
• Reporting Verb is changed into 'ordered, advised, requested, commanded, beg, forbade, suggested, proposed, assured, asked, reminded, warned, agreed, refused, promised', etc. 
 
• Inverted Commas will be removed. And conjunction 'to/not to' will be used. 
 
• *Example: *
 
 
• *He said, "Mohan, please bring me my towel." (Direct Speech)*
 
• *He requested Mohan to bring him his towel. (Indirect Speech)*
 
 
 
• **'Said to'** will be changed into **'told'** because **the reporting verb** has 'object'. 
 
• **Comma and inverted commas** will be removed. 
 
• **'To'** conjunction will be added.
 
• **'Go'** will be changed into** 'went'. **
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2. ****
 ​

Thus the correct sentence is:__** *"Mother told Kavya to switch off the light before she went to sleep."*

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Sarita said to me, “I’m glad I did not leave my village.”

options.text: Sarita told me I am glad she had not left her village.
Sarita told me that she was glad she had not left her village.
Sarita told me she is glad she had not left her village
Sarita told me she was glad she was not leaving her village.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Sarita told me that she was glad she had not left her village.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in Direct speech.
 
• Also, the tense of the sentence is a present tense hence, it is going to be changed into the past tense. Also, the second part is in the past tense. This is possible when the subject is in the present and talking about the past.
 
• In the given sentence, subject is 'Sarita' and the pronoun will be used according to the subject.
 
• Hence, **the correct indirect speech is**- *Sarita told me that she was glad she had not left her village.*

questions.question:
Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

Rita said to her friend, “My sister is performing on stage today for the first time.”

options.text: Rita told to her friend that her sister is performing on stage that day for the first time.
Rita told her friend that my sister was performing on stage today for the first time.
Rita said to her friend that my sister is performing on stage today for the first time.
Rita told her friend that her sister was performing on stage that day for the first time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **Rita told her friend that her sister was performing on stage that day for the first time. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from direct to indirect speech:
 
• When the direct speech is in an assertive form, we follow the steps given below:
 
 
• Convert the sentence in the direct speech into assertive.
 
• The tense of reported speech is changed only when the reporting verb is in the past tense. 
 
• The reporting verb said to is converted into told.
 
• The pronoun 'My' is replaced by 'her' accordingly. 
 
• The present continuous tense i.e. is performing will be changed to the past continuous tense i.e. was performing.
 
• Words showing time and place are changed accordingly. (today- that day)
 
 
 
• ​At last line up the remaining part.

 

Following these steps, we finally get- *Rita told her friend that her sister was performing on stage that day for the first time.*
